issues.evidence: All 205 annual entries have links, but 1822–2008 overwhelmingly use the same 198-page Garcia PDF with '#search=YEAR' fragments rather than page/section anchors or source quotations. The PDF itself contains multiple entries per year and its 2009 note states coverage through 2008. A browser text-search fragment cannot prove that each compound annual claim is documented. Targeted comparison did verify 1932 (PDF p.76, lines 2738–2744) and the River Plate treaty in 1969 (p.106, lines 3830–3837), but these spot checks do not validate the other annual claims.
issues.required_correction: Create a year-by-year evidence concordance with PDF page, exact dated passage and mapping of each material clause to that passage, separately citing non-Garcia claims and post-2008 direct sources; reconcile both locales.

issues.evidence: Garcia's PDF p.32 lines 1108–1109 expressly asserts that Brazil recognized the Argentine right to the islands in the 1833 entry, but provides no dated recognition instrument there. Current prose properly avoids presenting a signed act, yet describes FUNAG's retrospective chronology as mentioning support; the Garcia text is a stronger retrospective assertion than the independently demonstrated contemporaneous evidence. Neither source supplies the dated Brazilian act.
issues.required_correction: Distinguish Garcia's retrospective claim from contemporaneous diplomatic documentation, and avoid treating the year heading as proof of the date of a Brazilian recognition act.

issues.evidence: The 2026 entry combines January EU–Mercosur signature, May provisional application, and Brand Finance's 29th place. The two URLs are separately relevant but there is no quoted or dated source passage attached to each claim and no indication of ranking universe, methodology, survey reference period, or differentiation of brand perception from diplomatic effectiveness.
issues.required_correction: Provide precise EU Commission status passage and dated Brand Finance ranking/methodology with survey year, denominator and limitations, explicitly mapping each clause to its source.

issues.location: EN/PT chart of 11 UN Security Council terms, two tables, flow and map
issues.evidence: Both language files contain 205 annual entries and one chart, one flow, one map; this confirms structure, not that the chart's 11 mandates, denominators, source period and analytical transmission claims have been independently reconstructed. No full source-to-data concordance was completed in this review.
issues.required_correction: Attach auditable 11-term input series with official UN election dates and mandate years, reproduce the calculation, and map table/map/flow claims to underlying evidence in both locales.

verified_facts: Garcia PDF is 198 pages and states that its chronology was extended through 2008 (PDF p.3).
1932 Garcia PDF p.76 supports the São Paulo insurgents' unsuccessful US belligerency recognition and attempted arms acquisition.
1969 Garcia PDF p.106 supports signature of the River Plate Basin Treaty on 23 April.
Garcia PDF p.32 attributes Argentine territorial right recognition to Brazil under 1833 but does not identify the contemporaneous instrument.
EN and PT-BR have 205 annual bullet entries and matching targeted year wording; each has one chart, one flow and one map.
limitations: Only targeted Garcia passages were independently examined; no claim of 205 complete passage-level checks is made.
External institutional sources, 11-term chart calculations and Brand Finance methodology were not exhaustively verified in this run.
No reports, index, staging or approval record was edited.
